Claude Fable 5 is 24 hours old. Someone already cloned Minecraft in 20 minutes.

20 minutes. The original sold to Microsoft for $2.5 billion.

It didn’t stop there.

A 3D world running a full city simulator.
An agent beating Pokemon with nothing but its eyes.
Skyrim. 1 prompt.

Here’s what nobody says out loud:

None of these people are geniuses. None of them wrote code. They typed what they wanted in English.

The skill that used to cost a 4-year degree and $100,000 now costs a sentence.

So the gap isn’t talent anymore. It isn’t money. It’s who opens the tab in the first 24 hours and who keeps scrolling past it.

I’m starting from 0 today. Every build, every prompt, every dollar documented in public.

6 months from now this will be obvious to everyone. Today it’s just an open tab.

data.text:
CLAUDE FABLE 5 CHANGES THE GAME: FROM PROMPTS TO GOALS.

Until now, AI was a tool you micromanaged.

Prompt → Review → Prompt → Fix → Repeat.

Claude Fable 5 flips that model on its head.

Instead of giving AI step-by-step instructions, you give it a destination.

Then it plans, builds, tests, verifies, and iterates until the goal is complete.

The biggest shift isn't intelligence.

It's autonomy.

One demo built an entire productivity suite:

✅ Task manager
✅ Kanban board
✅ Calendar
✅ Notes app
✅ Pomodoro tracker
✅ Arcade game

...from a single high-level goal.

The new workflow is simple:

Old AI: "Do this next."

New AI: "Here's the outcome. Figure it out."

We're moving from prompting models to managing autonomous systems.

And that changes everything.
